reason: Both satisfy all hard requirements equally well (percentages sum correctly, valid RISK lines, halt metrics, decommissioning phase kept separate from the final migration batch), but Response B is a bit more internally consistent — its phase entry criteria explicitly reference the same 'see metrics below' thresholds defined in one Halt/Rollback Metrics section, whereas Response A mixes accuracy percentages in phase criteria with a differently-framed discrepancy percentage in its halt section. B also isolates high-risk enterprise/complex accounts into their own dedicated final phase with tailored entry criteria, which is a more risk-appropriate design than A folding enterprise accounts into the tail of its large general-availability phase.
